reading.body:
Electric utilities are the organized interest lobbying on the GRID Act, not AI companies. Every one of the 15 lobbying entries naming S. 3852 is an electric utility, a utility holding company, or a utility trade association.

The bill's own text tags it to energy and data centers, and its name states its purpose: insulating ratepayers from the cost of data center electricity demand. The sponsors are Josh Hawley, Richard Blumenthal, and Roger Marshall, a bipartisan group. The filings come from Portland General Electric, the Edison Electric Institute, Entergy, PPL, American Electric Power, CMS Energy, Xcel Energy, Puget Sound Energy, Exelon, Pinnacle West, and Pacific Gas and Electric. That is a national spread of investor-owned utilities, which are the parties that would build the generation and transmission AI data centers need and would recover the cost through rates.

For AI, the significance is who shows up. Compute buildout depends on power, and power depends on utilities that must justify new capacity in rate cases. When the utilities themselves lobby a bill about who pays for data center load, the cost allocation fight is live and the utilities are in it. The data does not say which side any of them took. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it.

What the data does not cover: the bill's text, its status beyond a latest date of 2026-02-11, any committee action, any vote, or any statement by a sponsor or a utility. It records 24 lobbying filings for 2025 or later, 15 of which are listed here with a named filer. It cannot show whether the lobbying changed the bill, whether the bill will move, or what any utility wants. It shows only that the utilities paying attention to data center power costs are paying attention to this bill.

summary: S. 3852, GRID Act Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers Act. Latest status date 2026-02-11. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 24 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
